A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPE research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original image/video evaluations, compression ablations, efficiency measurements, captioning results, and attention analyses in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds document/OCR/chart evaluations, VisionZip comparisons, model-size experiments, and further attention analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same positional-ID selection, dimension partitioning, rotation operator, and cascade compression procedure. VisionZip experiments apply the existing PPE operator without changing token selection or aggregation.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluated DocVQA, OCRBench, and ChartQA coverage, substantially extending testing of document layouts, text recognition, and chart reasoning. Existing training datasets, image/video benchmarks, and Flickr30k captioning evaluation remain.

E2.justification: The comparator roster expands by one compression family: VisionZip, evaluated with and without PPE in Tables 5 and 10. Existing Chat-UniVi, PACT, ToMe, and literature-based comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds training-free versus SFT comparisons and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct experiments. New settings include VisionZip projector-only training for one epoch on one-tenth of the curated data and a reduced 7B training budget. Table 1 also uses an expanded image-average benchmark mix, excluding OCRBench; the original experiments' settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine training dependence, model-size generalization, performance against dataset-average image resolution, and image attention under K=1, 16, and 32 (Section 4.4.3; Appendices A.4, A.9, A.10). Existing compression-ratio, aggregation-stage, captioning, and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added entropy and variance plots describe attention distributions, not uncertainty in benchmark performance.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial benchmark, VisionZip, 7B, and attention-analysis results while retaining earlier task-specific scores. Table 1's PPE image average changes from 81.15 to 79.32 because benchmark coverage changes, not because retained scores decline. Newly added delta annotations contain errors: Table 9 labels 42.10 versus 40.40 as +7.70.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1-7 remain unchanged. Appendix A.10 adds a qualitative frequency-allocation rationale for choosing K, without introducing a formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about parameter-free positional preservation, compatibility with existing compression methods, cascade compression, and performance retention. Added experiments support existing claims rather than redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 clarifies that training requirements depend on the underlying compression method, discusses a possible attention-perturbation explanation for VisionZip's 7B ChartQA decline, and expands the frequency-based explanation of K. It also asserts resolution robustness from dataset-level comparisons. Existing compression/fidelity limitations and failure cases remain.

D1.justification: V2 reports a project-code URL and documents new experiments' VisionZip selection ratios, projector-only training, sampling fractions, and reduced 7B data budget. The original learning rates, input limits, compression settings, and image/video K values were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds VisionZip, Kong et al.'s token-reduction discussion, Huang et al.'s positional-encoding analysis, and references for the three added benchmarks. These extend the supporting literature without substantially changing the paper's novelty positioning.

P1.justification: V2 revises the title, affiliation, and conference header; expands experimental explanations; and adds a training-requirements subsection and appendix analyses. Most existing prose and the main narrative organization remain intact, with corresponding cross-reference updates.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the experimental displays with training-regime and model-size comparison tables and new resolution and K-analysis figures. Table 1 gains benchmark rows, while retained tables receive caption clarifications or delta annotations. Figures 1-6 remain, although some displays relocate.

improvement.justification: The added document/chart evaluations, VisionZip comparisons, and training-dependence analysis test the existing layout-preservation and portability claims more directly; the code pointer also improves reproducibility information. These benefits are qualified by new arithmetic inconsistencies, including Table 9's +7.70 annotation for a 1.70 difference, and an overly broad resolution claim based on cross-dataset averages rather than controlled resizing. The revision provides a useful but limited net quality improvement.
